summary: Full RE of the EQUIP action (character-view main-menu option 0) in state 0x11. The dispatch at wpcvw 0x6a17 calls FUN_8e35, which the prior naming-pass labeled 'wpcvw_unequip_all_and_recompute' — that name is MISLEADING. FUN_8e35 is the WHOLE interactive EQUIP screen and it works in 3 phases: (PHASE 1) it UNEQUIPS EVERYTHING (writes 0xFF to all 8 body slots), clears the per-item 'equipped' bit (flags & 0xFE) on every inventory item, zeroes a batch of derived fields, and recomputes base AC via derived_stats_recompute_for_class (0x884f, the real AC/derived-stat function). (PHASE 2) it then walks the 8 BODY SLOTS in order 0..7 and, for each, gathers the list of carried items eligible for that slot (via FUN_835e, a candidate-collector that maps equip_slot->body_slot, enforces two-handed/shield exclusivity, and runs class/sex/race restriction checks), shows a left/right item PICKER inside the inventory panel, and on selection writes equipment[body]=inv_idx, re-sets the item 'equipped' bit, loads the item's full stats from the scenario item table (FUN_c31e/table 1) and APPLIES them (AC bonus to +0x4548-family, weapon damage/swings into the +0x44d8.. weapon-block for body 0/1, skill bonuses into +0x453a/+0x458a/+0x458b). (PHASE 3) a final 0..7 loop applies accumulated equip-granted SKILL/attribute bumps via a sub-picker (msg 0x17d). So EQUIP is NOT a single toggle — it is a guided 're-equip every slot from scratch' wizard. There is NO body-slot picker and NO equip<->unequip toggle inside this screen; the player just picks which item fills each slot. CRITICAL corrections: (a) FUN_8e35 is the equip screen, not an unequip-all helper; (b) the body-slot mapping in character-record-inventory-equipment.json is WRONG/shifted — the verified map is body0=weapon, body1=off-hand/shield, body2=cloak(equip5), body3=head(equip6), body4=chest(equip7), body5=legs(equip8), body6=hands(equip9), body7=feet(equip10); (c) helper names 0x835e/0x8dcd/0x81c2 are all misnamed.
method: PyGhidra DecompInterface (decompile.py) on FUN_8e35 (wpcvw 0x8e35, the EQUIP-action target), FUN_835e (candidate collector), FUN_884f (derived_stats_recompute_for_class = AC recompute), FUN_8dcd (item-label highlight renderer), FUN_81c2 (inventory compaction). Raw ndisasm of the EQUIP handler stub at 0x6a17 and of the equip_slot->body_slot dispatch table (CS:[bx+0xc9ae], file 0x844a, 17 entries) and its target stubs 0x83b1-0x8448. Cross-referenced: character-record-inventory-equipment.json (record field offsets, item-slot byte layout), wpcvw-character-view-ux.json (dispatch table, menu masks, *0x846 = highlight-blink flag), wpcvw-naming-pass.json (AC recompute 0xaa94 vs 0x884f, BSS layout). wpcvw runtime delta = 0x4564; thunk-delta law (thunk - 0xBA9C = wroot image, +0x200 = file).

findings.claim: EQUIP action (main-menu option 0) handler at wpcvw file 0x6a17 pushes three args and calls FUN_8e35, then jmp 0x6bad (back to the view main loop). Args, in C order (cdecl, pushed right-to-left at 0x6a17): param_1 = [bp-4] (the MAIN-PANEL window handle, local_4 in the view loop), param_2 = [bp-2] (the bottom PARTY-ROW window handle, local_6), param_3 = [bp+4] (the character slot index 0..5). There is NO msg_id and NO item-picker invoked by the handler itself — the entire UI is internal to FUN_8e35. EQUIP is enabled in all three context masks (camp/combat/dungeon) and is NOT gated by inv_count or is-active (it is always enabled).

evidence.details: Bytes at 0x6a17: ff 76 04 (push [bp+4]=slot) / ff 76 fc (push [bp-4]=mainPanel) / ff 76 fe (push [bp-2]=partyRow) / e8 12 24 (call 0x8e35) / 83 c4 06 (add sp,6) / e9 84 01 (jmp 0x6bad). Matches FUN_8e35 signature wpcvw_unequip_all_and_recompute(param_1=mainPanel, param_2=partyRow, param_3=slot). NOTE: in the FUN_8e35 decompile, param_1 is used as the inventory-panel render target window and param_2 as the picker/menu host; param_3 is the char slot used for all slot*0x1b0 record math.

findings.claim: FUN_8e35 @ wpcvw 0x8e35 is the complete EQUIP screen, NOT 'unequip all and recompute'. It runs three phases: PHASE 1 = full reset (unequip everything + clear equipped bits + zero derived fields + recompute base AC); PHASE 2 = for each of the 8 body slots (local_4 = 0..7), build a candidate list and let the player pick which carried item to equip in that slot; PHASE 3 = for each body slot, apply accumulated equip-granted skill/attribute bonuses via a small sub-picker. So choosing EQUIP from the menu drops the player into a per-slot 'fill this slot' wizard. There is no separate UNEQUIP menu option in the view — unequipping a single item is NOT possible from here; the player re-builds the whole loadout. (DROP, menu option 7, is the path that handles removing/dropping an item and is the one that enforces the cursed lockout.) RECOMMEND renaming FUN_8e35 to wpcvw_equip_screen.

evidence.details: PHASE 1 (function head): `for local_4 0..7: equipment[local_4] (at slot*0x1b0+0x44f8+local_4) := 0xff`; `for i 0..inv_count-1: item[i].flags (slot*0x1b0+i*8+0x442f) &= 0xfe` (clear equipped/cursed-bit0); `*(+0x458a):=0; *(+0x458b):=0`; `for i 0..13: *(+0x453a+i):=0`; then `derived_stats_recompute_for_class(slot)` (0x884f); then `ui_render_inventory_panel(param_1)`. PHASE 2 = outer `do { ... } while (local_4 < 8)` loop; PHASE 3 = second `do { ... } while (local_4 < 8)` loop with the msg-0x17d sub-picker. The outer-loop body collects candidates and runs an item picker per slot (see equip-candidate-collector and equip-picker-loop findings).

findings.supersedes: wpcvw-character-view-ux.json#action-equip-flow open question Q2; wpcvw-naming-pass.json name 'wpcvw_unequip_all_and_recompute' for 0x8e35

findings.claim: The EQUIP UX flow: on entry the engine (a) silently strips the character to nothing and recomputes base AC, then (b) for body slot 0, 1, 2, ... 7 in turn: it scans the inventory for items legal in that slot; if there is at least one candidate it draws them as a horizontal selectable row inside the MAIN-PANEL window (FUN_8e35 uses func_0x0000c6b2 to draw each candidate label + a per-slot title from msg 0x167 / msg 0x15e family) and lets the player move the cursor LEFT(key 2)/RIGHT(key 4) through the candidates plus an 'empty/skip' position (cursor index -1), committing with ENTER(key 5) or mouse click (*0x4fc4==1). The displayed highlight blinks via the *0x846 flag (see wpcvw-character-view-ux + wbase-picker findings: when *0x846==0 the highlight is drawn, else skipped — the blink). Picking 'empty' (local_c stays -1) leaves that body slot unequipped. After all 8 slots are filled the PHASE-3 skill-bonus sub-pickers run (msg 0x17d, a 2-wide grid). So: NO body-slot picker (slots are visited in fixed order), NO equip/unequip toggle, just one item-picker per body slot. Per-slot title text comes from indexed messages around 0x15e/0x167 (need msg.json confirmation for exact labels).

evidence.details: PHASE-2 loop body: `local_e = ui_render_spell_school_indicators(slot, local_4, local_22)` (candidate count + index array). `if (0 < local_e)`: clear+border the panel (func_0x0000ed5a(param_2,0x20), func_0x0000e5b5), load a title msg via func_0x0000c1f7(0x167/...) into local_82/local_d2, format with func_0x0000c05d, print via func_0x0000dfb9/df85, then `for local_6 0..local_e-1: func_0x0000bda7(param_1,...); func_0x0000dd53(...); func_0x0000df85(... item label at 0x55de+idx*0x10 ...); func_0x0000c6b2(...)` to render each candidate cell. Then the input loop `do { ... local_8 = input_poll_key_or_mouse_with_blink(); if (*0x4fc4==1) {mouse->commit}; else if (local_8==2) {LEFT}; else if (local_8==4) {RIGHT} } while (local_8 != 5)`. local_c is the chosen candidate index, -1 = empty/skip. Highlight render gated on `*0x846 == 0`.

findings.claim: FUN_835e (wpcvw 0x835e, misnamed 'ui_render_spell_school_indicators') is the per-body-slot candidate collector. Signature: collect(charSlot=param_1, bodySlot=param_2, out_indices=param_3). It zeroes the 10-entry output array, then iterates inventory items i=0..inv_count-1; for each item it (1) maps the item's equip_slot byte (item+0x442c) to a target body slot via a 17-entry CS jump table at CS:[bx+0xc9ae] (file 0x844a); (2) if that target body slot != param_2 (the slot being filled), skips; (3) otherwise runs THREE restriction checks via func_0x0000e34b against the character's class (+0x4587), sex (+0x4585), race (+0x4586) — all three must return 1 (allowed); (4) if all pass, appends the inventory index i to out_indices and increments the count. Returns the count. The class/sex/race gating is how CLASS_LOCKED-type restrictions are actually enforced at equip time (the item-flag 0x40 is NOT directly tested here — restriction is data-driven through func_0x0000e34b reading the item's allowed-class/sex/race bitmasks loaded from the scenario item table).

evidence.details: Decompile: out array param_3 init to 0xffff x10; loop while i < *(slot*0x1b0+0x4594) [inv_count]; equip_slot = item[i]+0x442c; `if (equip_slot < 0x11) jump CS:[equip_slot*2+0xc9ae]` else indirect dispatch (the >=0x11 path leads to a separate jump at 0x8474, CS:[uVar1*2-0x3652] — an out-of-range/scroll handler). Each jump-table stub sets [bp-6]=target_body_slot. At 0x85d2: `if ([bp-6] == param_2)` then run func_0x0000e34b(local_1e, class@+0x4587)==1 && func_0x0000e34b(local_1c, sex@+0x4585)==1 && func_0x0000e34b(local_1a, race@+0x4586)==1 -> append i to out array, inc count. func_0x0000c31e(table=1, item_id) is called to load the item record into local_54 first so e34b can read its restriction fields.

findings.claim: VERIFIED equip_slot (item byte +0x442c, cached from scenario.dbs byte 60) -> body-slot mapping, decoded from the 17-entry jump table at file 0x844a (CS 0xc9ae) and its target stubs 0x83b1-0x8448. body0=MAIN WEAPON; body1=OFF-HAND/SHIELD; body2=CLOAK; body3=HEAD; body4=CHEST/BODY ARMOR; body5=LEGS; body6=HANDS/GLOVES; body7=FEET/BOOTS. Per-equip_slot: equip_slot 0,1,2,3,0xc,0x10 -> stub 0x83b1: target=body0 if the slot being filled is 0; OR target=body1 if the slot being filled is 1 AND item flags&0x04 (a thrown/dual-wieldable weapon can go in the off-hand). equip_slot 4 (ranged) -> body1. equip_slot 5 (cloak) -> body2. equip_slot 6 (head) -> body3. equip_slot 7 (chest) -> body4. equip_slot 8 (legs) -> body5. equip_slot 9 (hands) -> body6. equip_slot 0xa (feet) -> body7. equip_slot 0xb (shield) -> body1. equip_slot 0xd,0xe,0xf -> body1 only if flags&0x04 (else not equippable here = scroll/consumable). This CONTRADICTS and CORRECTS character-record-inventory-equipment.json#equipment-array-offset, which listed body[1]=shield, body[2]=head, body[3]=body, body[4]=legs, body[5]=hands, body[6]=feet, body[7]=cloak — that was off by one starting at cloak. The correct order is weapon/offhand/cloak/head/chest/legs/hands/feet.

evidence.details: Jump table at file 0x844a (17 LE u16 = CS addrs; file_off = CS - 0x4564): slots 0/1/2/3/0xc/0x10 -> 0x83b1; 4 -> 0x83ea (body=1); 5 -> 0x83f2 (body=2); 6 -> 0x83fa (body=3); 7 -> 0x8402 (body=4); 8 -> 0x8409 (body=5); 9 -> 0x8410 (body=6); 0xa -> 0x8417 (body=7); 0xb -> 0x841e (body=1); 0xd/0xe/0xf -> 0x8425 (body=1 if flags&0x04). Stub 0x83b1: `cmp [bp+6],0 -> body=0`; `cmp [bp+6],1; test item.flags&0x04 -> body=1`. Stub 0x8425: `test item.flags&0x04 -> body=1` else stays 0xffff (not equippable). The two-hand/shield exclusivity block at 0x8479 further validates body-slot 1 against the already-equipped weapon's sprite_idx (item+0x442d) values 0xb/0xc/0xd/0x16/0x17/0x53. [bp+6] is the target body slot param_2.

findings.supersedes: character-record-inventory-equipment.json#equipment-array-offset body_slot_mapping (was off-by-one for cloak..feet; medium-confidence guess now corrected)

findings.claim: Two-handed/shield exclusivity is enforced for body slot 1 (off-hand) by the block at FUN_835e 0x8479-0x85a3 and by a fixup at the end of the equip write in FUN_8e35. When the candidate collector is asked for body-slot-1 candidates (param_2==1), it reads the currently-equipped MAIN WEAPON (equipment[0] at +0x44f8), and if the weapon's sprite/type byte (+0x442d) is one of a set of 'occupies both hands' values it disqualifies off-hand candidates (the equip_slot 0/1/2/3 'thrown can dual-wield' path only allows body1 when item flags&0x04). Separately, in FUN_8e35 after a body-slot-0 (weapon) equip, the code checks `if (local_4 == 0 && (equippedWeapon.flags & 0x08) != 0) local_4 = 1;` — i.e. equipping a TWO-HANDED weapon (flag 0x08) advances the loop to body slot 1 and effectively consumes the off-hand slot, so the player is never offered a shield/off-hand pick when a 2H weapon is wielded. So a 2H weapon occupies BOTH body0 (weapon) and body1 (off-hand).

evidence.details: In FUN_8e35, just before the final per-slot render: `if ((local_4 == 0) && ((item[local_a].flags @ slot*0x1b0+local_a*8+0x442f & 8) != 0)) { local_4 = 1; }` — local_4 is the body-slot loop var, local_a is the chosen inventory index. flag 0x08 = two-handed (per character-record finding). FUN_835e 0x8479: when param_2==1, loads equipment[0] (+0x44f8), and compares the equipped weapon's +0x442d byte against 0xb/0x16/0xd/0x17/0xc/0x53 to decide if an off-hand item is compatible; mismatches set [bp-6]=0xffff (disqualify).

findings.claim: On a committed pick (local_c != -1, local_a = inventory index of chosen item, local_4 = body slot), the equip WRITE is: (1) equipment[local_4] (byte at slot*0x1b0 + 0x44f8 + local_4) := local_a; (2) item[local_a].flags (slot*0x1b0+local_a*8+0x442f) |= 1 (set the 'equipped' bit — bit0, the same bit PHASE 1 cleared for all items); (3) load the item's full stats from the scenario item table via func_0x0000c31e(table=1, item_id) into a temp record (yielding local_e6=weight?, local_e4=AC bonus, local_e3, local_ea/local_e9/local_e2/local_112/local_110 = weapon block fields, local_ee, abStack_10a[14] = skill bonus array, local_e8/local_e7 = derived caps); (4) accumulate auStack_32[local_4] := local_e6 (for the PHASE-3 skill sub-picker). The previous occupant of a body slot is NOT swapped back individually — PHASE 1 already cleared ALL slots to 0xFF up front, so each PHASE-2 pick fills a fresh empty slot. NOTE: items themselves are never moved out of inventory by equipping (equipment[] just holds an index); equipped vs carried is purely the equipment[] index + the flags bit0.

evidence.details: `if (local_c != -1) { local_a = local_22[local_c]; equipment[local_4] (local_4[slot*0x1b0+0x44f8]) = (char)local_a; iVar4 = slot*0x1b0 + local_a*8; *(iVar4+0x442f) |= 1; func_0x0000c31e(1, &local_12a, item_id=*(iVar4+0x4428), 0); auStack_32[local_4] = local_e6; ... }`. The locals local_e4/local_ea/etc are filled by the c31e item-record load (the temp item record). Because PHASE 1 set every equipment[] byte to 0xFF and cleared every item flags bit0, there is no per-pick swap-back.

findings.claim: AC and weapon-stat recompute on equip: (A) BASE AC is recomputed ONCE in PHASE 1 by derived_stats_recompute_for_class (FUN_884f @ 0x884f) which writes AC into +0x4548 (the primary AC byte) and broadcasts it to the per-row/positional AC bytes +0x4549..+0x454f. (B) Per equipped item, the item's AC bonus (local_e4, the loaded item record's AC field) is SUBTRACTED from the AC field (lower AC = better, Wizardry convention): for body slots 0 and 1 it subtracts from +0x4549 (`*(+0x4549) -= local_e4`); for body slots 2..7 it subtracts from +0x4548 directly (`equipment-row AC at +0x4548+local_4 -= local_e4`, i.e. each armor slot 2..7 reduces its own positional AC byte). (C) For weapon slots (body 0 and 1), the chosen item's WEAPON BLOCK is written into the per-hand weapon struct at slot*0x1b0 + local_4*0x10 + 0x44dc.. (+0x44dc 8-byte to-hit/skill array from abStack_10a, +0x44e2 swings, +0x44e4, +0x44e5, +0x44e6 = damage * -5 / accumulate, +0x44d8/+0x44da = damage dice, +0x44e7 = flags), with class-conditional bonuses (class 0xc/0xd = priest/ninja-style get STR/5+5 to swings). (D) Skill caps +0x458a/+0x458b are raised to the item's required values (max). NOTE: FUN_884f (0x884f) is the function this screen uses for the base recompute; the separate FUN_aa94 documented in wpcvw-naming-pass#fn-ac-recomputation is the LEVEL-UP AC recompute — they are different functions but both write +0x4548.

evidence.details: PHASE 1: `derived_stats_recompute_for_class(slot)` then `ui_render_inventory_panel`. FUN_884f writes `*(slot*0x1b0+0x4548)` (base AC=10 then SPD/race/class adjustments) and propagates to +0x4549..+0x454f via the `iStack_4 = 3; do *(slot*0x1b0+iStack_4+0x4548) = *(slot*0x1b0+0x4548); while < 8` loop. Per-item in FUN_8e35: `if (local_4==0 || local_4==1) { *(+0x4549) -= local_e4; ...weapon block writes to +local_4*0x10+0x44dc.. ; } else { equipment-AC: *(slot*0x1b0+0x4548+local_4) -= local_e4; }`. Damage field: `if (local_ee==4) *(+0x44e6)=local_e3*-5 else *(+0x44e6)+=local_e3*-5`. Skill caps: `*(+0x458a)=max(*(+0x458a),local_e8); *(+0x458b)=max(*(+0x458b),local_e7)`.

open_followups: Q: Exact field meanings of local_e4 (AC bonus) vs local_e6 (weight? skill-grant id) vs local_e3 (damage) vs the +0x44dc weapon block are inferred from the c31e item-record layout; cross-check against the scenario item record byte map (scenario.dbs 74-byte item records) to lock each offset.

Q: Is the AC subtract-vs-add sign correct (lower AC = better)? The code subtracts local_e4 from the AC field; confirm local_e4 is non-negative for armor with a live DOSBox check (equip leather cuirass -> AC drops).

findings.claim: PHASE 3 (second 0..7 body-slot loop in FUN_8e35) applies equip-granted skill/attribute bumps. For each body slot that accumulated a positive grant (auStack_32[local_4] > 0), it opens a small 2-column grid sub-picker (ui_menu_picker_grid with msg base 0x17d) listing the skill/attribute the item grants, prompts the player, and on confirm (local_c==1): if the grant code < 9 it bumps an attribute (`*(slot*0x1b0+0x4514+(grant-1))++` if < 0x14 cap — the 6 attributes STR..SPD live at +0x4514..+0x4519); else if grant-9 < 5 it does an indirect dispatch (CS:[(grant-9)*2-0x22c5]) into a special-grant handler; then decrements the item quantity (inventory_decrement_quantity) and re-renders the full sheet. This is how 'use-on-equip' or attribute-granting items apply their effect. (Most stock items grant nothing, so this loop is usually a no-op.)

evidence.details: Second loop: `for local_4 0..7: if (0 < auStack_32[local_4]) { clear+border panel; build msg 0x17c/0x17d; local_c = ui_menu_picker_grid(param_2, 0x17d, &local_132, count, 2, 3, 1); if (local_c==1) { if (auStack_32[local_4] < 9) { idx=auStack_32[local_4]-1; if (*(slot*0x1b0+0x4514+idx) < 0x14) (*(... +0x4514+idx))++; } else if (auStack_32[local_4]-9 < 5) (*(code*)CS:[(auStack_32[local_4]-9)*2-0x22c5])(); inventory_decrement_quantity(slot, equipment[local_4]); ui_render_full_character_sheet(param_1); } } }`. auStack_32 was loaded with local_e6 from the item record during PHASE 2.

open_followups: Q: What is the grant-code (auStack_32 / item record local_e6) semantics? Values 1..8 map to attribute index, 9..13 to special handlers via CS:[(n-9)*2-0x22c5]. Resolve that 5-entry jump table (file = CS - 0x4564) to name the special grants.

findings.claim: GUARDS on equip: (1) CLASS/SEX/RACE restriction is the only equip-time block, enforced data-drivenly by the three func_0x0000e34b checks in FUN_835e (class +0x4587, sex +0x4585, race +0x4586). An item failing any check is simply NOT offered as a candidate for any slot. The item-flag 0x40 (CLASS_LOCKED) is not directly tested in the equip path — restriction lives in the item's allowed-class/sex/race bitmasks read via e34b. (2) CURSED (flags 0x01/0x02) does NOT block EQUIP — in fact PHASE 1 clears flag bit0 on every item and the equip write re-sets bit0 (`|= 1`) as the 'equipped' marker. The cursed lockout is enforced ELSEWHERE: the DROP action (menu option 7, file 0x6a86) tests `item.flags & 0x43` and beeps/refuses if set (per wpcvw-character-view-ux#action-drop-cursed-check-correction). Because this EQUIP screen always re-equips from scratch, a cursed item that the player chooses NOT to re-pick stays unequipped — but the player also cannot DROP it. (3) NO explicit STR/level numeric requirement gate was found in the equip candidate path; weapon usability differences are expressed through the per-class weapon-block bonuses, not a hard block.

evidence.details: FUN_835e candidate filter: three func_0x0000e34b(buf, char_class/sex/race) == 1 checks gate appending the candidate. FUN_8e35 PHASE 1 clears `flags &= 0xfe` for all items, then on equip sets `flags |= 1`. No `and 0x01/0x02/0x40` test exists in FUN_8e35 or FUN_835e. The cursed `& 0x43` test is in the DROP handler 0x6a86 (separate, documented in wpcvw-character-view-ux.json). bit0 is doing double duty as 'equipped marker' in this overlay's runtime record, distinct from the on-disk CURSED meaning — careful: PHASE 1's `&= 0xfe` clears the equipped marker, NOT a permanent cursed flag wipe (the high cursed bit 0x02 is untouched).

open_followups: Q: func_0x0000e34b is the restriction-bitmask matcher; RE its body (resolve thunk: e34b is intra-overlay wpcvw 0xe34b? or a thunk — check) to confirm exactly which item record fields encode allowed class/sex/race and how they combine. The item flag 0x40 CLASS_LOCKED relationship to the e34b bitmask needs nailing down.

Q: Confirm bit0 double-meaning: on disk 0x01 = cursed-bit0, at runtime in this record it is also reused as the equipped marker. Verify a cursed item (disk flag 0x01) still works through this screen — does PHASE-1's &0xfe corrupt the persisted cursed state when the record is saved back? (Possible bug or intentional: cursed-ness may be re-derived from the item table on load.)

findings.claim: FUN_81c2 (wpcvw 0x81c2, misnamed 'ui_render_equip_swap_window') is an INVENTORY COMPACTION / reorder routine, NOT a window renderer. It walks the 8 equipment slots; for each equipped item it bubbles that item's 8-byte inventory record toward the front of the inventory grid (so equipped items occupy the lowest inventory indices), shifting other items up by one slot (rep-movsw of 4 words = 8 bytes per slot) and rewriting any equipment[] index that pointed at a shifted slot. It also moves the parallel name-string buffer (0x55de + idx*0x10) and a per-item word table at 0x567e. RECOMMEND renaming to wpcvw_compact_equipped_to_front (or similar). This is invoked from the EQUIP/inventory flows to keep equipped gear contiguous in the grid for display.

evidence.details: Decompile: `local_10 = 0; for local_c 0..7: idx = equipment[local_c] (+0x44f8+local_c); if (idx != 0xff) { save item record bytes (local_a/_8/_6/_4 = item[idx] 4 words at +0x4428..+0x442e), copy name; for local_e = idx down to >local_10: shift item[local_e] := item[local_e-1] (rep movsw 4 words), shift name buffer, fix any equipment[] entry == local_e-1 to local_e; place saved record at item[local_10]; local_10++ }`. Pure data reorg, no ui_window_create call.

findings.claim: FUN_8dcd (wpcvw 0x8dcd, misnamed 'derived_stats_recompute_for_race') is the EQUIP candidate-row HIGHLIGHT renderer.
